Location: The Alliance pipeline draws from 59 receipt points, largely concentrated near the northern end of the system in northeastern B.C. and northwestern Alberta. The Alliance pipeline continues through Saskatchewan and connects to the U.S. section of the Alliance pipeline at the Canada-U.S. border near Elmore, Saskatchewan.
Pipeline capacity: Capacity on the Alliance pipeline is measured at specific key points. At the border key point near Elmore, Saskatchewan, the capacity is approximately 1.6 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d).

Location: The Aurora pipeline starts near Carway, Alberta and ends at the Canada–U.S. border.
Transported commodity: Natural gas liquids, condensate, light sweet crude, and light sour crude
Pipeline capacity: Approximately 45 thousand barrels per day (Mb/d)

Location: The Emera Brunswick pipeline extends from the Saint John LNG liquefied natural gas import terminal near Saint John, New Brunswick through southwest New Brunswick to an interconnection with the Maritimes & Northeast pipeline (M&NP) near St. Stephen, New Brunswick.
Pipeline capacity: Approximately 0.85 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d)

Location: The Cochin pipeline extends from Fort Saskatchewan, Alberta to the Canada-U.S. border near Elmore, Saskatchewan.
Pipeline capacity: Approximately 95 thousand barrels per day (Mb/d)

CER-regulated company: Enbridge Bakken Pipeline Company Inc., on behalf of Enbridge Bakken Pipeline Limited Partnership
Location: The Enbridge Bakken pipeline extends from the Canada-U.S. border between Saskatchewan and North Dakota to the delivery point located near Cromer, Manitoba.
Pipeline capacity: Approximately 145 thousand barrels per day (Mb/d)

Location: Enbridge Line 9 originates at Sarnia, Ontario, and terminates at Montreal, Quebec.
Pipeline capacity: Approximately 300 thousand barrels per day (Mb/d)

Location: The Enbridge Mainline originates in Edmonton, Alberta and extends east across the Prairies. The pipeline crosses the Canada-U.S. border near Gretna, Manitoba, where it joins with the Enbridge Lakehead system (U.S. section of the Mainline) and ultimately terminates near Sarnia, Ontario.
Transported commodity: Crude oil, refined petroleum products, natural gas liquids
Pipeline capacity: The nameplate capacity from Gretna (ex-Gretna) is 3.22 million barrels per day (MMb/d). In 2022, available capacity ex-Gretna has ranged between a low of 3.17 MMb/d in August to a high of 3.32 MMb/d in June. The nameplate capacity into-Sarnia is 1.04 MMb/d. In 2022, available capacity at into-Sarnia has ranged from 1.03 MMb/d in June to 1.09 MMb/d in November.
Major interconnected pipelines: Wascana pipeline, Enbridge Bakken system, Enbridge Lakehead system, Keystone pipeline, Express pipeline,  Enbridge Line 9

Location: The Canadian portion of the Express pipeline extends from Hardisty, Alberta to the Canada-U.S. border near Wild Horse, Alberta.
Transported commodity: Light, medium, heavy and super-heavy crude oil
Pipeline capacity: Approximately 310 thousand barrels per day (Mb/d)

Location: The Foothills system starts from Caroline, Alberta and extends southwest to Kingsgate, British Columbia and southeast to Monchy, Saskatchewan.
Pipeline capacity: Capacity on the Foothills pipeline is measured at specific key points. At Monchy, the capacity is approximately 2.2 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d). At Kingsgate, the capacity is approximately 2.8 Bcf/d.
Major interconnected pipelines: NGTL system, Northern Border pipeline, Gas Transmission Northwest pipeline

Location: The Genesis pipeline is a small system located near Corunna, Ontario.
Transported commodity: Natural gas liquids, feedstock for the NOVA Chemicals’ Corunna facility
Pipeline capacity: Approximately 37 thousand barrels per day (Mb/d)

Location: The Canadian portion of the Keystone pipeline runs from Hardisty, Alberta east across Saskatchewan and Manitoba, before turning south and crossing the Canada-U.S. border near Haskett, Manitoba into North Dakota.
Pipeline capacity: Keystone’s nameplate capacity pipeline is 591 thousand barrels per day (Mb/d). In 2022, available capacity ranged from 585 Mb/d in August to 643 Mb/d in September. Keystone has been able to increase its capacity in recent years through the use of Drag Reducing Agents, some of which increases nameplate capacity and some of which increases available capacity.

Location: The Many Islands pipeline system consists of 12 pipelines crossing the Alberta/Saskatchewan border, the Manitoba/Saskatchewan border and the Saskatchewan/United States border.
Pipeline capacity: Pipelines in the Many Islands pipeline system have various capacities.
Major interconnected pipelines: Gathering lines in Alberta, NGTL system, TransGas pipeline system, Williston Basin Interstate pipeline system, NorthWestern Energy pipeline system

Location: The main receipt point on the Milk River pipeline is the interconnect with the Bow River pipeline near Milk River, Alberta. The main delivery point is the interconnect with the Front Range pipeline at the Canada/U.S. border west of Coutts, Alberta.
Transported commodity: A variety of crude oil streams
Pipeline capacity: Approximately 97.9 thousand barrels per day (Mb/d)
Major interconnected pipelines: Bow River pipeline, Front Range pipeline

Location: M&NP starts at the Canada-U.S. border near St. Stephen, New Brunswick and runs through New Brunswick and Nova Scotia. M&NP laterals extend to Point Tupper, Goldboro, Halifax and Saint John.
Pipeline capacity: Approximately 0.5 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d)
Major interconnected pipelines: Sable Offshore Energy project, Deep Panuke project, M&NP (U.S. section)

Location: The main receipt point of the Montreal pipeline is located in South Portland, Maine, and the main delivery point is located in Montreal, Quebec.
Pipeline capacity: Approximately 223 thousand barrels per day (Mb/d)

CER-regulated company: NGTL GP Ltd. as general partner on behalf of NGTL Limited Partnership
Location: NGTL is a large natural gas gathering and transportation system with receipt and delivery locations located across the province of Alberta, as well as Northeastern British Columbia.
Pipeline capacity: Capacity on the NGTL is measured at specific key points. At Upstream of James River, the capacity is approximately 12.4 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d). At East Gate, the capacity is approximately 4.8 Bcf/d. At West Gate, the capacity is approximately 3.0 Bcf/d.
Major interconnected pipelines: TC Canadian Mainline, Foothills system, Wescoast / Enbridge BC pipeline, Alliance pipeline

Location: The Norman Wells pipeline extends from Norman Wells, Northwest Territories to Zama in northern Alberta, where it connects with the Alberta oil pipeline network.
Pipeline capacity: Approximately 16.4 thousand barrels per day (Mb/d)

CER-regulated company: Enbridge Southern Lights GP Inc. on behalf of Enbridge Southern Lights LP
Location: The Southern Lights pipeline extends from the Manitoba/U.S. border, across Saskatchewan, to Edmonton, Alberta.
Transported commodity: Diluent for blending bitumen and heavy oil
Pipeline capacity: Approximately 195 thousand barrels per day (Mb/d)

Location: The TC Canadian Mainline extends from the Alberta/Saskatchewan border across Saskatchewan, Manitoba and Ontario, and through a portion of Quebec.
Pipeline capacity: Capacity on the TC Canadian Mainline is variable depending on the specific location key points. At Prairies, the capacity is approximately 6.2 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d). At Iroquois, the capacity is approximately 0.6 Bcf/d.
Major interconnected pipelines: NGTL system, TQM pipeline, Viking Gas Transmission pipeline, Great Lakes Gas Transmission pipeline, Empire pipeline, Tennessee Gas pipeline, National Fuel Gas pipeline, Iroquois Gas Transmission system, St. Lawrence Gas Company, North Country Gas pipeline and Vermont Gas systems

CER-regulated company: Trans Québec and Maritimes Pipeline Inc.
Location: The TQM pipeline extends from an interconnect with the TC Canadian Mainline near Saint Lazare, Quebec, to a point near Quebec City in the municipality of Lévis on the south shore of the St. Lawrence River. TQM also extends from Terrebonne, north of Montreal, to a point on the Canada-U.S. border near East Hereford, Quebec.
Pipeline capacity: Capacity on the TQM pipeline is measured at specific key points. At East Hereford, the capacity is approximately 0.4 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d). At Saint Lazare & Sabrevois, the capacity is approximately 1.0 Bcf/d.
Major interconnected pipelines: TC Canadian Mainline, Portland Natural Gas Transmission system

Location: The Trans Mountain pipeline extends from Edmonton, Alberta to Burnaby, British Columbia, with delivery points in Kamloops, Sumas, and Burnaby, B.C.
Transported commodity: Crude oil and refined petroleum products
Pipeline capacity: The Trans Mountain Expanded System has a nameplate capacity of approximately 890 thousand barrels per day (Mb/d). The Trans Mountain Expansion Project came online on 1 May 2024. Prior to that date, Trans Mountain’s nameplate capacity was approximately 300 Mb/d.

Parent company: Imperial Oil Limited, Royal Dutch Shell Plc, Suncor Energy Inc.
Location: The Trans-Northern pipeline extends from Nanticoke, Ontario to Montreal, Quebec. There are delivery points along the route, including Oakville, Toronto, Ottawa, Maitland, Belleville, Cornwall and Kingston in Ontario, as well as Montreal and Dorval in Quebec.
Transported commodity: Refined petroleum products such as gasoline, diesel fuel, aviation fuel and heating fuel
Pipeline capacity: Capacity varies across each line segment of the Trans-Northern pipeline. From Nanticoke to Oakville, the capacity is 105 thousand barrels per day (Mb/d). From Oakville to North Toronto, the capacity is 105 Mb/d. From Montreal to Farran’s point, the capacity is 132 Mb/d. From Farran’s Point to Ottawa, the capacity is 60 Mb/d. From Farran’s Point to Belleville, the capacity is 72 Mb/d. From Belleville to North Toronto, the capacity is 63 Mb/d.
Major interconnected pipelines: Three other petroleum products pipelines (two Sun-Canadian and Enbridge’s Line 8)

Location: The Canadian portion of the Vector pipeline system extends from the Ontario/Michigan border to Dawn, Ontario. Dawn is the largest natural gas storage area in Canada.
Pipeline capacity: Approximately 1.745 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d)

Location: The Wascana pipeline extends from the Canada-U.S. border in Montana to the Plains Terminal in Regina, Saskatchewan.
Pipeline capacity: Approximately 40 thousand barrels per day (Mb/d)

Location: The Westcoast pipeline extends from a point in northern British Columbia near Fort Nelson south to Sumas. Two segments of the Westcoast pipeline also cross the British Columbia and Alberta border near Dawson Creek and Boundary Lake.
Pipeline capacity: Capacity on the Westcoast pipeline is measured at specific key points. At Huntingdon/Fortis BC Lower Mainland, the capacity is approximately 1.7 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d).
Major interconnected pipelines: Williams Northwest pipeline, NGTL system, FortisBC local distribution, Southern Crossing pipeline

Location: The Westspur pipeline extends from points in Saskatchewan to the main delivery point, which is the Enbridge Mainline near Cromer, Manitoba.
Pipeline capacity: Approximately 247.4 thousand barrels per day (Mb/d)
Major interconnected pipelines: Saskatchewan Gathering system, Enbridge Canadian Mainline
